title: Release run citations in docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md and .quest history go stale (misleading, not wrong) after a workflow re-run
description:
DISCOVERED 2026-09-17, relayed from opum-cli-e2e (via opum-agent, filed fleet-wide as OPAG-165) and independently confirmed against this repo.

MECHANISM. `gh run view <id>` / `gh api repos/.../actions/runs/<id>` and `gh run download <id>` all resolve to a run's LATEST attempt, not the attempt that originally produced a citation. Re-running a workflow (even a cancelled/failed re-run) replaces that run id's default answer AND its downloadable artifacts -- GitHub exposes no `/attempts/N/artifacts` endpoint (404), so a superseded attempt's original artifacts are permanently unreachable through the API once a later attempt has uploaded artifacts under the same names. Only a copy taken at citation time survives.

CONFIRMED INSTANCE. Release run 34968280818 (v0.7.0, dispatched publish:false) was attempt-1 success 2026-09-15T12:20:29Z, then attempt-2 cancelled 2026-09-16T23:42:26Z (triggered by jeremy-newhouse via gh api: triggering_actor confirmed). Four of six platform-qualification jobs succeeded again on attempt 2; win32-x64 and win32-arm64 were cancelled. All six `ladybug-package-qualification-*` artifacts were replaced by attempt-2's uploads; opum-cli-e2e's independent byte comparison found five of six identical across attempts, but win32-x64's `stderrSha256` differs and its producing job was the cancelled one -- so the artifact `gh run download 34968280818` now serves for win32-x64 is output from a job that did not complete successfully, filed under the same run id and filename as the original.

EXPOSURE IN THIS REPO, found by grepping for the run id and for bare `actions/runs/<id>` / `gh run view` style citations (docs/, CHANGELOG.md, README.md, .quest/):

1. docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md -- the MAINTAINED release-evidence-of-record doc -- cites run `34968280818` bare at least 6 times (lines ~27-67), including as the source of the six `ladybug-package-qualification-<name>-34968280818` reports whose digests it says were independently verified. That verification happened 2026-09-15, against attempt 1 (correct, before the re-run) -- the CLAIM is not false. But the citation is no longer self-verifying: a future reader re-checking it via `gh run view`/`gh run download` today gets attempt 2, and for win32-x64 specifically gets a report from a cancelled job wearing the same name.

2. .quest/completed/LCLI-496.json (Done, closed 2026-09-15 -- this repo's own 0.7.0 release-gate task) cites the same run id the same bare way in implementationNotes and finalSummary, written when attempt 1 was the only attempt and the citation was accurate.

RELATED PRIOR ART IN THIS REPO: docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md already documents an analogous (history-rewrite-caused, not re-run-caused) case for 0.6.0's run 34393976910 going 404, concluding "this is not repaired, and will not be" and pointing at lore-cli-release-truth.md's digests as the thing to trust instead of the CI link. That precedent is exactly the right shape for this case too: don't try to repair the citation, add a note explaining why the bare form no longer resolves the way it did, and point at the durable evidence (digests, retained artifact copies) instead.

NOT IN SCOPE / NOT CLAIMED: nothing about the published 0.7.0 packages is wrong. Attempt 1 was success, five of six qualification reports are byte-identical across both attempts, and 0.7.0's release-truth claims (digest verification, propagation timing, etc.) were made and verified against attempt 1's real data before the re-run happened.

THREE THINGS TO DECIDE (opum-cli-e2e explicitly left these to the owning repo rather than prescribing):
(a) Add a clarifying addendum to lore-cli-release-truth.md's 0.7.0 section noting the 2026-09-16 re-run and that citations should now be read as attempt-1 (with the attempt-scoped API form for anyone re-verifying).
(b) Append (never rewrite) a similar clarifying note to the closed LCLI-496.json record -- consistent with this repo's own history-integrity rule (CLAUDE.md: 'Rewriting a Done record to remove a word falsifies it').
(c) A repo-level decision, out of scope for a docs-only task: whether release.yml (or a runbook convention) should guard against/warn on re-running a workflow already dispatched on a release tag, given the destructive side effect on artifacts. This task does not decide that -- flag it, at most, as a recommendation.

acceptanceCriteria.text: docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md 0.7.0 section carries a dated addendum explaining the 2026-09-16 attempt-2 re-run, that bare gh run view/download now resolve to attempt 2, and that the digest verification claims were made against attempt 1 before the re-run
LCLI-496.json (closed) gets an appended clarifying note (via quest task edit --add-note, not a rewrite of existing fields) pointing at the addendum above -- original text untouched
A recommendation (not necessarily an implementation) is recorded on whether release.yml or the release runbook should discourage/guard re-running a workflow already dispatched on a release tag

implementationNotes:
RECOMMENDATION (AC3), not implemented here -- scope discipline: neither opum-cli-e2e nor opum-agent asked for a release.yml change, both explicitly left it to this repo to judge, and CLAUDE.md's own repo profile requires a reviewer pass on anything touching release.yml -- too large a change to fold into a docs-only task silently.

Recommend a CHEAP guard over a structural one: add a step early in release.yml's package/qualification jobs that checks `github.run_attempt != '1'` and, if so, fails loudly with a message pointing at this task and the release-truth addendum, requiring a human to acknowledge (e.g. re-dispatch with an explicit `confirm_rerun: true` workflow_dispatch input) before the matrix runs again on a tag ref. This is enforcement rather than a runbook note, but it is a small, local, reviewable diff -- not a redesign of the release pipeline. Filed as a recommendation rather than a task because it is a judgment call about how much friction a release operator should face, which is the user's to make, not mine to default into existing by writing the code.

Also worth recording for whoever picks this up: the same hazard applies in principle to any CI run cited as evidence, not just release.yml -- ci.yml push/pull_request runs cited in CLAUDE.md's repo profile (e.g. the dev/main promotion examples) have the identical bare-run-id fragility if anyone ever re-runs one of those. Lower stakes (no irreplaceable artifacts riding on them, illustrative rather than evidentiary), so not raised as its own finding, but the mechanism generalizes.

FOLLOW-UP 2026-09-17: opum-cli-e2e's own message prompted them to sweep all 15 run ids cited in their baselines/README.md, using this task as the trigger. Their result, relayed here for anyone who later wonders whether the fleet-wide version of this hazard got checked: 7 of 15 already 404 in all three repos (all lore-cli/quest-cli, all predating the 2026-09-10 repo recreation, OPAG-70 -- unrecoverable, nothing to do), 1 changed answer without changing id (34968280818, this task), 1 was already correctly attempt-qualified in their record (34801853367, "attempt 3", predating the rule by about a year), and the remaining 6 are attempt-1/success and self-verifying today. They fixed their own doc the same way (dated addendum, not a rewrite) and refined the wording I should carry here too: sharpened the addendum below to separate run METADATA (attempt-scoped, answers correctly forever) from run ARTIFACTS (not attempt-scoped, /attempts/N/artifacts is a hard 404) -- citing attempts/1 makes a claim VERIFIABLE, it does not make evidence RETRIEVABLE. Only a copy taken at citation time does that.
finalSummary: Addendum added to docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md's 0.7.0 section explaining the 2026-09-16 attempt-2 re-run of release run 34968280818 and why bare gh run view/download now resolve to the cancelled attempt instead of attempt 1; clarifying note appended (not rewritten) to the closed LCLI-496 record pointing at that addendum; a cheap-guard recommendation for release.yml recorded rather than implemented, since neither reporting peer asked for one and it needs its own reviewer pass. lore check --plain: 80 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
